root_cause.text: In `virtio_transport_recv_enqueue()` the vsock/virtio RX path assumed any small `skb` was linear and safe to coalesce into the previous packet, but after `MSG_ZEROCOPY` support some small skbs became non-linear, so copying them via the linear data area lost payload and could append uninitialized kernel memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the coalescing condition from `if (len <= GOOD_COPY_LEN && !skb_queue_empty(&vvs->rx_queue))` to also require `!skb_is_nonlinear(skb)`, and the commit message explicitly says the bug was caused by the “assumption that a small skb will always be linear” becoming incorrect with `MSG_ZEROCOPY`, leading to “data is lost” and “uninitialized kernel memory” being appended.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid coalescing non-linear skb payloads in virtio vsock receive enqueue to correctly handle zerocopy packets.
intent_record.what: The receive enqueue path in virtio_transport_recv_enqueue() was changed so the small-packet copy-into-last-queued-buffer optimization now also requires !skb_is_nonlinear(skb). A comment was added clarifying that non-linear skbs, such as zerocopy packets, store payload in skb_shinfo and should be skipped by this optimization.
intent_record.how: At runtime, small incoming packets will still be coalesced into the previous queued skb, but only if the new skb is linear. Non-linear skbs will no longer be incorrectly treated as directly copyable payload buffers, preventing misuse of their data layout and preserving correct handling of zerocopy/non-linear packet payloads.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid coalescing non-linear skb payloads in virtio vsock receive enqueue to correctly handle zerocopy packets.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents coalescing small but non-linear skbs in virtio vsock RX enqueue, which avoids losing payload or appending uninitialized memory after MSG_ZEROCOPY support.

candidates.rationale: This condition blindly treats all small received skbs as safe to coalesce into the previous packet. The root cause is that some small skbs can be non-linear after MSG_ZEROCOPY, so this size-only check directly enables the unsafe copy path that can drop payload or append uninitialized data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This size-only coalescing check assumes any small skb is linear and safe to append to the previous packet. After MSG_ZEROCOPY support, small skbs may be non-linear, so this condition enables the unsafe receive-enqueue copy path that can lose payload or copy uninitialized kernel memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `virtio_transport_recv_enqueue()`. The code explicitly tries to merge small receive packets into the last queued buffer: `if (len <= GOOD_COPY_LEN && !skb_queue_empty(&vvs->rx_queue)) { ... if (skb->len < skb_tailroom(last_skb) && !(le32_to_cpu(last_hdr->flags) & VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM)) { memcpy(skb_put(last_skb, skb->len), skb->data, skb->len); ... } }`. This is the coalescing path implicated by the root cause, because it copies from `skb->data` without checking whether the skb is linear. There is no fix here to reject non-linear skbs or to safely copy from the full skb payload; the code still assumes `skb->data` is the correct source for small packets and appends them directly. So the buggy construct is present and the fix is not present in this commit.
